Information Boxes: 
 Health and Learning Accommodations
1. Bringing prescribed medication to Japan
If you need to bring prescribed medication to Japan, with a dosage in excess of one month,  you are 
required to apply and obtain a document called "Yu -nyu Kakunin -sho" (Import Confirmation of 
Medication) before leaving Japan, and declare it at Japan Customs. Details and instructions on how to 
obtain the document can be found through the links below, with online applications now being possible. 
 Information provided by the Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare, Japan:  
- https://www.mhlw.go.jp/english/policy/health-medical/pharmaceuticals/01.html (English)
- https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/iyakuhin/kojinyunyu/topics/tp01
0401-1.html (Japanese)
 On-line Application:  https://impconf.mhlw.go.jp/aicpte/page/login.jsp?lang=en/#
2. Nagoya University Ability Support Centre
Nagoya University makes every effort to ensure that students with disabilities have equal access and are not 
disadvantaged in their learning environment. Students who require study/classroom accommodations are 
invited to consult the Abilities Support Centre and submit an application by the end of February (April 
admissions), or the end of August (Autumn admissions). 
- https://www.gakuso.provost.nagoya-u.ac.jp/osd/en_index.html (English)
- https://www.gakuso.provost.nagoya-u.ac.jp/osd/index.html (Japanese)
 Email: soudan@gakuso.provost.nagoya-u.ac.jp (English language service available)
3. Na
goya University Advising & Counseling Services (ACS)
Qualified professionals at ACS offer confidential counseling to help students with mental health, stress, 
and cross‑cultural adjustment so they can feel supported and thrive at Nagoya University. 
https://acs.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/  (English) 
https://acs.iee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/ (Japanese)
